title: Cold rebuild: size the pool to lose a zone
summary: Rebuild the zone-loss sizing from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You wrote **Size the pool to lose a zone** in *Availability maths and failure
domains*. Now write it again from an **empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests
are the ones you passed the first time.
Why: in a design review nobody hands you the formula. If you can rebuild it cold, you can say it out loud
when someone asks "and what happens when a zone goes?". If you get stuck, go back to the lesson and try again

steps.prompt: A service needs 36 instances to carry its peak at the target utilisation. It runs in 4 zones. How many instances should it run so that losing any one zone still leaves 36?
steps.explain: 36 instances must survive across 3 zones: 12 per zone. Run 12 in each of the 4 zones: 48. That is 33% extra, against 100% extra for the same service on 2 zones.

steps.prompt: Checkout runs in 3 zones at 55% CPU at peak. One zone fails. Roughly what CPU do the survivors run at?
steps.explain: 55% x 3 / 2 = 82.5%. It fits, but queueing at 83% makes p99 noticeably worse: plan the target after the loss, not just the fit.

steps.title: Cold rebuild: size the pool to lose a zone
prompt: - `double MaxUtilToSurvive(int zones)`: the highest utilisation at which losing one zone still fits:
- `int InstancesNeeded(double peakQps, double qpsPerInstance, int zones)`: instances in total, spread evenly,
so that after losing one zone the rest still serve `peakQps` at `qpsPerInstance` each. Instances per zone are
rounded up. Fewer than 2 zones throws `ArgumentException`.
